episode_title: Who Owns Marketing at Your RIA? A Guide for Firm Leaders (Ep. 71)

real_qa.q: What are the main reasons RIA firms lack clear marketing ownership?
real_qa.r: Many founders built their firms through informal sales and hustle rather than formal marketing, so structured marketing roles weren't considered necessary. Firms often struggle to justify the cost of a full-time CMO when revenue may not yet support it. Additionally, advisors frequently entered the industry to do financial planning and trading, not marketing—creating resistance to the role. Finally, many firms don't understand the long-term value of marketing strategy.
real_qa.requete: why RIA firms lack marketing ownership

real_qa.q: According to the Entrepreneurial Operating System framework, who should own the marketing and sales seat at an RIA?
real_qa.r: In the EOS accountability chart, there should be a dedicated person owning the marketing and sales seat. However, Kristen observes that in practice, the visionary (CEO) often becomes a bottleneck with great ideas but poor execution, or the integrator (COO) adds marketing as another task to their list rather than treating it as core strategy—creating activity without direction.
real_qa.requete: EOS framework marketing sales seat RIA

real_qa.q: What is the difference between owning marketing and simply executing marketing tasks?
real_qa.r: An owner of marketing is responsible for upholding brand standards, positioning, and personality across all channels. They set goals, track results, manage budgets, ensure staff and vendors stay aligned, and drive what the firm will and won't do. Task execution alone lacks this strategic oversight and accountability—many partially developed efforts never get finished or seen because nobody owned them end-to-end.

real_qa.q: What are the realistic options for assigning marketing ownership at an RIA?
real_qa.r: An RIA can have the founder own marketing if they have genuine interest and time. An internal hire like a marketing coordinator or manager can execute well under a strategist. An agency—especially one understanding financial services like Out and About Communications—can partner from strategy through execution. Or firms can hire a fractional CMO who provides strategic leadership part-time at lower cost than a full-time executive.
real_qa.requete: RIA marketing ownership options founder agency CMO

real_qa.q: Why is vendor or agency oversight essential even after hiring outside help for marketing?
real_qa.r: Even when hiring an SEO agency or ad vendor, someone inside the firm must direct and oversee them to ensure accountability. The firm owner or marketing leader must verify that the vendor's work is on-brand, helpful, and compliant with regulations—you cannot simply hand off and forget about it.

guest.bio_context: Kristen launched her own RIA and now guides countless financial advisors through growth strategies, marketing, sales, and leadership insights. She offers fractional CMO services to firms seeking strategic marketing ownership without full-time cost.
